name: Sugar Hackberry

facts.how: Crunch whole (thin sweet skin over a crunchy nut) or blend into bars
facts.when: September into winter, hanging on the twig
facts.where: Every fence line and vacant lot in Texas
facts.value: Sugar, fat, and protein in one package, a true trail food

caution: The berry is mostly seed; eat it like a crunchy snack, not a mouthful of soft fruit, or blend and strain. Warty gray bark is the tree's fingerprint.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: The tree everyone has and nobody planted: gray bark studded with corky warts, sandpaper leaves, and winter twigs beaded with orange berries.

sections.title: On the trail
sections.body: Hackberries are candy that crunches. Native Texans pounded them whole into cakes, sugar, fat, and protein in one wild bar.
